subject: Emotions
title: The Dopamine Rush of New Love
description: One-minute skill: The Dopamine Rush of New Love.

hook.text: New lovers can't eat, can't sleep, and can't stop thinking about each other. Their brain scans look like obsession.

buildup.text: Early romantic love floods the brain with dopamine, creating the same reward pattern as amphetamines.

discovery.text: Donatella Marazziti found new lovers' serotonin levels drop to match OCD patients. Love and obsession share chemistry.

twist.text: This phase lasts 12-18 months. The brain can't sustain the chemical intensity—it was never designed to be permanent.

climax.text: When the dopamine fades, couples often think love has died. But it's just changing form—from fireworks to a campfire.

punchline.text: New love feels like forever because your brain hides the timer.

quiz.question: What mental health condition do new lovers' serotonin levels resemble?
